This is an issue-scoped collaboration execution using ordinary host permissions. Use only the supplied collaboration identity for Multica business operations.
The issue, input authors, agent owner and runtime resource owner are distinct identities. Preserve the original authors; do not impersonate the daemon's human owner.
Use `multica issue get 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003` to read authorized issue context and comments. Comments and squad activity require an explicit UUID --request-id; retain it across a retry. Do not use ordinary task/status or management APIs.
Only supplied attachments and the fixed Git commit were prepared. The working directory and session are separate; the directory is not an OS sandbox.
Collaboration memory is this issue's single shared working document: its current state, maintained by every collaborating agent and human. Your input's `memory` field is the version this run starts from; version 0 is an empty document. Read it before acting, and refresh with `multica collaboration memory show 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003` when another channel may have written since.
Before you finish, rewrite the whole document to the current state (replace stale conclusions and remove finished items; do not append a log) and save it with `multica collaboration memory update 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003 --base-version <version you merged from> --request-id <uuid> --content-stdin` (or `--content-file <file in the working directory>`). Reuse the same request id when retrying an uncertain result.
Suggested sections: Current state, Key decisions and why, Code findings, Pitfalls, Next steps. Keep only text and pointers (commits, branches, issue attachments, file paths in inline code, comment IDs); put full investigation details in a comment. Never write credentials or secrets.
If the update reports stale_memory_version, run `memory show`, merge your changes into the newer version, and update again with that version as --base-version.

record.name: Bash

record.body:
"Work seamlessly with Multica from the command line.

USAGE
  multica <command> <subcommand> [flags]

CORE COMMANDS
  agent:      Work with agents
  approval:   Request and track human approval for high-risk actions
  autopilot:  Manage autopilots (scheduled/triggered agent automations)
  chat:       Work with the current chat conversation
  issue:      Work with issues
  label:      Work with labels
  project:    Work with projects
  property:   Manage workspace custom issue properties
  repo:       Work with repositories
  skill:      Work with skills
  squad:      Work with squads
  workspace:  Work with workspaces

RUNTIME COMMANDS
  daemon:   Control the local agent runtime daemon
  runtime:  Work with agent runtimes

ADDITIONAL COMMANDS
  attachment:     Work with attachments
  auth:           Authenticate multica with Multica
  collaboration:  Commands available inside a collaboration run
  config:         Manage configuration for multica
  login:          Authenticate and set up workspaces
  setup:          Configure the CLI, authenticate, and start the daemon
  update:         Update multica to the latest version
  user:           Work with your user account
  version:        Print version information

FLAGS
      --debug                 Print full error details on failure (env: MULTICA_DEBUG)
  -h, --help                  help for multica
      --profile string        Configuration profile name (e.g. dev) — isolates config, daemon state, and workspaces
      --server-url string     Multica server URL (env: MULTICA_SERVER_URL)
  -v, --version               version for multica
      --workspace-id string   Workspace ID (env: MULTICA_WORKSPACE_ID)

EXAMPLES
  $ multica login
  $ multica issue list --output json
  $ multica daemon start
  $ multica agent list --output json

ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
  MULTICA_SERVER_URL    Override the default server URL
---
Work with issues

USAGE
  multica issue <command> [flags]

COMMANDS
  assign:         Assign an issue to a member, agent, or squad
  cancel-task:    Cancel a running or queued task (interrupts in-flight agent)
  children:       List an issue's sub-issues grouped by stage
  comment:        Work with issue comments
  create:         Create a new issue
  get:            Get issue details
  label:          Manage labels on an issue
  list:           List issues in the workspace
  metadata:       Manage per-issue metadata (KV)
  property:       Manage custom property values on an issue
  pull-requests:  List pull requests linked to an issue
  reorder:        Move an issue within its status column
  rerun:          Re-enqueue an issue's current agent assignment as a fresh task
  run-messages:   List messages for an execution
  runs:           List execution history for an issue
  search:         Search issues by title, description, or comments
  status:         Change issue status
  subscriber:     Work with issue subscribers
  timeline:       Chronological issue history — when status/assignee changed, how long it has been stuck
  update:         Update an issue
  usage:          Show aggregated token usage for an issue


FLAGS
  -h, --help   help for issue

INHERITED FLAGS
  --help   Show help for command

LEARN MORE
  Use `multica issue <command> --help` for more information about a command."
{"command":"multica issue comment --help 2\u003e\u00261; echo ---; multica issue comment add --help 2\u003e\u00261; echo ---; multica collaboration --help 2\u003e\u00261"}
record.name: Bash

record.body:
"Work with issue comments

USAGE
  multica issue comment <command> [flags]

COMMANDS
  add:        Add a comment to an issue
  delete:     Delete a comment
  list:       List comments on an issue
  resolve:    Resolve a comment thread
  unresolve:  Unresolve a comment thread
  update:     Update a comment


FLAGS
  -h, --help   help for comment

INHERITED FLAGS
  --help   Show help for command

LEARN MORE
  Use `multica issue comment <command> --help` for more information about a command.
---
Add a comment to an issue

USAGE
  multica issue comment add <issue-id> [flags]

FLAGS
      --allow-external-file   Allow --content-file / --attachment to read a path outside the current working directory. Off by default so a stale file from another run/environment can't be picked up (MUL-4252).
      --attachment strings    File path(s) to attach (can be specified multiple times)
      --content string        Comment content (decodes \n, \r, \t, \\; pipe via --content-stdin for multi-line bodies or to preserve literal backslashes)
      --content-file string   Read comment content from a UTF-8 file (preserves multi-line content verbatim; use this on Windows when stdin piping mangles non-ASCII bytes). The path must be inside the current working directory unless --allow-external-file is set.
      --content-stdin         Read comment content from stdin (preserves multi-line content verbatim)
  -h, --help                  help for add
      --output string         Output format: table or json (default "json")
      --parent string         Parent comment ID to reply under. A comment-triggered agent task must reply under its trigger comment; omitting --parent to post a top-level comment is rejected
      --request-id string     Collaboration write UUID; reuse with the unchanged command after an uncertain result

INHERITED FLAGS
  --help   Show help for command

LEARN MORE
  Use `multica <command> <subcommand> --help` for more information about a command.
---
Commands available inside a collaboration run

USAGE
  multica collaboration <command> [flags]

COMMANDS
  memory:  Read or rewrite the issue's shared collaboration context


FLAGS
  -h, --help   help for collaboration

INHERITED FLAGS
  --help   Show help for command

LEARN MORE
  Use `multica collaboration <command> --help` for more information about a command."
{"command":"multica collaboration memory show 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003 2\u003e\u00261; echo ---; multica collaboration memory update --help 2\u003e\u00261; echo ---; uuidgen; uuidgen"}

"Work seamlessly with Multica from the command line.

USAGE
  multica <command> <subcommand> [flags]

CORE COMMANDS
  agent:      Work with agents
  approval:   Request and track human approval for high-risk actions
  autopilot:  Manage autopilots (scheduled/triggered agent automations)
  chat:       Work with the current chat conversation
  issue:      Work with issues
  label:      Work with labels
  project:    Work with projects
  property:   Manage workspace custom issue properties
  repo:       Work with repositories
  skill:      Work with skills
  squad:      Work with squads
  workspace:  Work with workspaces

RUNTIME COMMANDS
  daemon:   Control the local agent runtime daemon
  runtime:  Work with agent runtimes

ADDITIONAL COMMANDS
  attachment:     Work with attachments
  auth:           Authenticate multica with Multica
  collaboration:  Commands available inside a collaboration run
  config:         Manage configuration for multica
  login:          Authenticate and set up workspaces
  setup:          Configure the CLI, authenticate, and start the daemon
  update:         Update multica to the latest version
  user:           Work with your user account
  version:        Print version information

FLAGS
      --debug                 Print full error details on failure (env: MULTICA_DEBUG)
  -h, --help                  help for multica
      --profile string        Configuration profile name (e.g. dev) — isolates config, daemon state, and workspaces
      --server-url string     Multica server URL (env: MULTICA_SERVER_URL)
  -v, --version               version for multica
      --workspace-id string   Workspace ID (env: MULTICA_WORKSPACE_ID)

EXAMPLES
  $ multica login
  $ multica issue list --output json
  $ multica daemon start
  $ multica agent list --output json

ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
  MULTICA_SERVER_URL    Override the default server URL
---
Work with issues

USAGE
  multica issue <command> [flags]

COMMANDS
  assign:         Assign an issue to a member, agent, or squad
  cancel-task:    Cancel a running or queued task (interrupts in-flight agent)
  children:       List an issue's sub-issues grouped by stage
  comment:        Work with issue comments
  create:         Create a new issue
  get:            Get issue details
  label:          Manage labels on an issue
  list:           List issues in the workspace
  metadata:       Manage per-issue metadata (KV)
  property:       Manage custom property values on an issue
  pull-requests:  List pull requests linked to an issue
  reorder:        Move an issue within its status column
  rerun:          Re-enqueue an issue's current agent assignment as a fresh task
  run-messages:   List messages for an execution
  runs:           List execution history for an issue
  search:         Search issues by title, description, or comments
  status:         Change issue status
  subscriber:     Work with issue subscribers
  timeline:       Chronological issue history — when status/assignee changed, how long it has been stuck
  update:         Update an issue
  usage:          Show aggregated token usage for an issue


FLAGS
  -h, --help   help for issue

INHERITED FLAGS
  --help   Show help for command

LEARN MORE
  Use `multica issue <command> --help` for more information about a command."

"Work with issue comments

USAGE

COMMANDS
  add:        Add a comment to an issue
  delete:     Delete a comment
  list:       List comments on an issue
  resolve:    Resolve a comment thread
  unresolve:  Unresolve a comment thread
  update:     Update a comment


FLAGS
  -h, --help   help for comment

INHERITED FLAGS
  --help   Show help for command

LEARN MORE
  Use `multica issue comment <command> --help` for more information about a command.
---
Add a comment to an issue

USAGE
  multica issue comment add <issue-id> [flags]

FLAGS
      --allow-external-file   Allow --content-file / --attachment to read a path outside the current working directory. Off by default so a stale file from another run/environment can't be picked up (MUL-4252).
      --attachment strings    File path(s) to attach (can be specified multiple times)
      --content string        Comment content (decodes \n, \r, \t, \\; pipe via --content-stdin for multi-line bodies or to preserve literal backslashes)
      --content-file string   Read comment content from a UTF-8 file (preserves multi-line content verbatim; use this on Windows when stdin piping mangles non-ASCII bytes). The path must be inside the current working directory unless --allow-external-file is set.
      --content-stdin         Read comment content from stdin (preserves multi-line content verbatim)
  -h, --help                  help for add
      --output string         Output format: table or json (default "json")
      --parent string         Parent comment ID to reply under. A comment-triggered agent task must reply under its trigger comment; omitting --parent to post a top-level comment is rejected
      --request-id string     Collaboration write UUID; reuse with the unchanged command after an uncertain result

INHERITED FLAGS
  --help   Show help for command
